selection.rule: Dependency-complete first 24 questions from the question-sheet selection order.

questions.question: In the comparison, what did the king place in the care of each of the two men?
questions.answer: Each man was given an estate along with the equipment and resources needed to run it.

questions.question: Why did the king send a high-ranking representative to the two men?
questions.answer: He sent him to deliver a merciful message about how they could protect what had been entrusted to them and gain from it.

questions.question: According to the message, what would the king do with the property if they gave it back to him?
questions.answer: He would preserve it for them, keep it from being wasted, and later return it in a better form.

questions.question: What did the king promise concerning the tools and machines?
questions.answer: He promised they would be used in his service and that their return would be multiplied greatly.

questions.question: Until what point would they keep the income and benefit from the arrangement?
questions.answer: They would keep it until the time when military service ended.

questions.question: What would happen to the valuable instruments if the offer was rejected?
questions.answer: They would lose their worth instead of being put to good use.

questions.question: What higher status did the king promise to the one who accepted?
questions.answer: He would serve under the king with honor instead of remaining in a low and restricted position.

questions.question: What personal qualities led the second man to refuse?
questions.answer: He was proud, self-centered, and morally careless.

questions.question: What happened to the first man after his acceptance?
questions.answer: He rose to a high rank, received the king’s favor, and lived in happiness.

questions.question: What contrast between the two men forms the main lesson of the passage?
questions.answer: Accepting the king’s offer brings honor, safety, and reward, while rejecting it brings loss, humiliation, and suffering.

questions.question: How many men are at the center of the comparison, and what was each one given?
questions.answer: There are two men, and each received an estate with the necessary tools and resources.

questions.question: What does the king’s mercy show in the way he dealt with the two men?
questions.answer: It shows that he wanted their good and offered them a way to avoid loss and gain much more.

questions.question: What future benefit did the king promise after the time of conflict had passed?
questions.answer: He promised to return what they had entrusted in a better state than before.

questions.question: In what way would the use of the workshops and tools become more beneficial under the king’s arrangement?
questions.answer: Their use would bring a vastly multiplied return and profit.

questions.question: What practical help did the king promise in addition to payment?
questions.answer: He promised to cover expenses, provide equipment, and still let them receive the gains.

questions.question: If someone rejected the king’s offer, what did the king say would happen to the property itself?
questions.answer: It would slip away and be lost without any lasting benefit.

questions.question: How would refusal affect the value of the fine equipment?
questions.answer: Those precious items would become worthless.

questions.question: What distinction did the king make between low service and honored service?
questions.answer: He contrasted an ordinary and constrained status with an elevated position under a great ruler.

questions.question: How did the second man’s character distort his judgment?
questions.answer: His pride and attachment to pleasure made him reject what would have saved him.

questions.question: What final outcomes prove that the first decision was right and the second wrong?
questions.answer: The first man ended in honor and happiness, while the second ended in loss, blame, and suffering.

questions.question: What basic situation begins the comparison in this passage?
questions.answer: A king entrusts two men with estates and the means to manage them.

questions.question: Who delivered the king’s message to the two men?
questions.answer: A noble representative sent by the king.

questions.question: What did the king ask the two men to do with what had been entrusted to them?
questions.answer: He asked them to return it to him through a voluntary transfer.

questions.question: How did the king increase the attractiveness of the offer regarding the tools and machinery?
questions.answer: He promised that using them under his authority would bring far greater returns.
